hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: The decimal $0.2$ is one fifth. Think about how many fifths are in one whole, and then in five wholes.
Dividing by a decimal is awkward. Both numbers can be scaled by the same power of ten without changing the quotient.
Multiply both $5$ and $0.2$ by $10$, which moves each decimal point one place. The problem becomes $50 \div 2$.

explanation: Make the divisor a whole number by multiplying both numbers by $10$. This keeps the quotient the same.
After both decimal points move one place, $5 \div 0.2$ becomes $50 \div 2$.
Dividing the whole numbers now gives $50 \div 2 = 25$.
So $5 \div 0.2 = 25$. You can check by multiplying back: $0.2 \times 25 = 5$.
